conflicts.fact: When and where the guttation experiment is set up and read, and what covers the seedling
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the guttation experiment (Predict-Observe-Explain) is set up in the next lesson (Lesson 2). Lesson 2 says it is set up at the end of Day 1 (with a bell jar or plastic bag) and read on Day 2, and also has learners predict what they will see 'under the bell jar tonight'. Lesson 3 says a POE guttation setup, with a potted seedling covered by a clear polythene bag overnight, is started again in Lesson 3 for observation the next morning, as if it were a new experiment, so it is unclear which lesson actually does it.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson answers the insoluble-waste question and what Lesson 1 says plants do with wastes
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says plants store insoluble wastes such as resin, latex and gum in tissues, and the next question it raises is how remaining wastes leave the plant (guttation droplets). Lesson 2 raises 'what happens to insoluble wastes' as the new question, although Lesson 1 already claimed they are stored in tissues like bark, vacuoles and old leaves. Lesson 2 also says its guttation/exudation explanation covers the oozing sap, yet leaves insoluble wastes unexplained.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson explained Euphorbia latex ooze (exudation) and where guttation was evidenced
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5's DQB example cites 'Why do Euphorbia trees ooze? L3, exudation of latex', but exudation of gums, resins and latex was explained in Lesson 2 (Lesson 3 covers crystals and tissue fall).

conflicts.fact: Where wastes are stored (dead vs. non-vital tissues) and what plants lack
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says wastes are stored in living tissues such as bark, vacuoles and old leaves. Lesson 5 says plants store wastes in dead tissues, and its Learned section says plants lack excretory organs because they 'produce few toxic wastes', whereas Lesson 3 says wastes are stored in non-vital organs and Lesson 4 says they accumulate in latex vessels and vacuoles (living structures).

conflicts.fact: Composition of guttation fluid and seasonal leaf fall
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 describes guttation as liquid with dissolved salts and sugars from hydathodes, in the context of waste removal, while Lesson 1 treats the droplets as an unexplained route; Lesson 5 says leaf fall occurs in the dry season while the phenomenon describes seasonal leaf drop without specifying; Lesson 5 also calls the Lesson 1 model a 'drawing of how a plant gets rid of wastes' while Lesson 1 describes revising a Day 1 comparative human-plant diagram.
